h1: Press brake tooling — EUROSTAMP punches, dies and adapters for every clamping style, made in Italy
intro: NovoTech sells and supports EUROSTAMP press brake tooling in Canada: punches, dies, holders, adapters and clamping made in Italy by a company that has built nothing but press brake tooling since 1970. Six pages cover the range — European-style (Amada-Promecam) punches and dies for most press brakes in Canadian shops, Trumpf and Wila-style tooling, Bystronic and LVD-style tooling, American-style tooling with the .500″ tang, and the holders, adapters and accessories that let one press brake run another style's tools. Every table gives the angle, height, tip radius or V opening and load rating of each tool in inches and millimetres, with DXF profiles to load into your CNC. Below the range: how to choose a V opening and the tonnage chart for air bending.

C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened 55 – 60 HRC up to 3 mm (.118″) deep; special tools to your drawing

faq.q: Which tooling fits my press brake?
faq.a: It depends on the clamping, not the brand of the machine. Most press brakes in Canadian shops — Amada, Accurpress, Baykal, Dener, Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Yawei and many more — clamp European-style (Amada-Promecam) tools. Trumpf, Darley and Safan use Trumpf or Wila (New Standard) clamping; Bystronic and Beyeler use type R, RF or RF-A; LVD has its own; and many older North American brakes take American-style tools with a .500″ tang. Send us the model of your brake or a photo of the clamp and a tool, and we confirm before you order.

faq.q: How do I choose the V opening?
faq.a: Start with V = 8 × the sheet thickness for mild steel up to about 1/2″ — V24 (about 1″) for 1/8″, V50 (2″) for 1/4″ — and 10 to 12 × for heavier plate. Aluminum works with 6 ×, stainless with 8 – 10 ×. The inside radius comes out at about 1/6 of the V and the shortest flange you can bend at about 0.7 × V. The guide and the tonnage chart below work through it.

faq.q: How much tonnage does a bend need?
faq.a: For 90° air bending of mild steel, tons per foot ≈ 575 × t² ÷ V, with the thickness t and the V opening in inches: 1/4″ in a 2″ V needs about 18 US tons per foot of bend, so a 10 ft bend needs about 180 tons. Stainless needs about 1.5 times as much, soft aluminum about half. The tooling must be rated above the tonnage per foot, and the press brake above the total.

faq.q: What do the load ratings in the tables mean?
faq.a: The maximum force the tool takes per unit of length — EUROSTAMP gives it in tonnes per metre, we add US tons per foot. If a bend needs 15 tons per foot, use a punch and a die rated above 15 US t/ft (45 t/m). Concentrated loads on a short piece of tool are the usual way tools crack: a 1 ft part bent with 30 tons puts 30 tons per foot on the tool.

Yes. EUROSTAMP's technical department designs special punches and dies — profiles, radii, offsets, combined tools — for parts standard tooling cannot bend. Send us the part drawing and the press brake model, and we come back with a proposal and a price.

faq.q: What steel is the tooling made of?
faq.a: C45 medium-carbon steel, raw or tempered, and Italian 42CrMo4 chrome-molybdenum steel for the heavier and slimmer tools. The working surfaces are induction-hardened to 55 – 60 HRC up to 3 mm (.118″) deep, so the tip and shoulders resist wear while the body stays tough. The ESH insert dies are nitrided all over to 65 HRC.

faq.q: Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?
faq.a: Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.
